  The dispatch engine shows completed invocations as still active. Root cause: in _spawnInvocation (dispatch.ts), the cleanup chain is shadowMutex.runExclusive(runInvocation).then(drainQueues).finally(cleanupActiveDetails). The .then() calls _drainQueues which spawns the NEXT invocation via shadowMutex.runExclusive — but .finally() only runs after .then() completes. This means the old invocation's activeInvocationDetails entry persists until the next invocation finishes. Fix: move activeInvocationDetails.delete and activeCount decrement into the .runExclusive callback (after emitting the event), BEFORE the drain step. The .then should only handle draining, and .finally should only handle abort controller cleanup.

fix(dispatch): clean up active fleet tracking before draining next invocation

The dispatch engine's _spawnInvocation cleanup chain had a timing issue where
activeInvocationDetails and activeCount were cleaned up in .then()/.finally()
handlers that only ran after the next invocation completed (since .then()
called _drainQueues which acquired the shadowMutex for the next invocation).

Moved activeCount decrement and activeInvocationDetails.delete into the
runExclusive callback so they execute while still holding the mutex, before
_drainQueues can spawn the next invocation. This prevents completed agents
from appearing as still active in the fleet status page.

EOF
